newsitem.title: UK: Novorossiisk pipeline reopens, storm damages berth.
newsitem.headline: Novorossiisk pipeline reopens, storm damages berth.

text.p: The main crude pipeline feeding Russia's main oil export terminal of Novorossiisk reopened late on Sunday after five days of scheduled maintenance, a shipping source said on Monday.
"The pipeline is back up...It was down since last Wednesday morning, I believe," the source said, adding the pipeline was working on full rate since midnight local Novorossiisk time.

"To be honest there wasn't a large amount of disruption to loading because there was so much bad weather that the port was closed anyway and it was just routine maintenance being done on the pipeline, a fairly standard thing that happens monthly."
The pipeline has a capacity of about 600,000 barrels per day. It was shut for maintenance for around 74 hours in early March.
The source said Novorossiisk's berth two was damaged during a strong storm that hit the port over the weekend.
"We haven't got the full information on it, we just know that the berth is closed at the moment. It was actually a vessel alongside which did the damage to the berth," the source added.

The port itself shut down from 10.30 p.m. Novorossiisk local time on Thursday until 1.20 a.m. on Sunday due to wind and swell. Swell also caused the port to close from 5.30 p.m. on Sunday to 7.30 a.m. Monday.
The Baltic port of Ventspils was closed on Monday while the Black sea ports of Odessa and Tuapse were open.
